question: A 15-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his father 10 minutes after falling into a frozen lake during ice fishing. He was in the water for less than 1 minute before his father managed to pull him out. On arrival, his clothes are still wet and he appears scared. His body temperature is 36.2°C (97.1°F), pulse is 102/min, blood pressure is 133/88 mm Hg. Which of the following mechanisms contributes most to maintaining this patient's core body temperature?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fall into frozen lake" -> "Rapid heat loss due to cold water" -> "Decreased core body temperature" -> "Body temperature 36.2°C" -> "Body initiates compensatory mechanisms" -> "Involuntary muscular contractions" -> "Contributes to maintaining core body temperature" -> 80%

analysis: In this scenario, the most significant mechanism contributing to maintaining the patient's core body temperature is involuntary muscular contractions, also known as shivering. Shivering generates heat through muscle activity, helping to increase the body's temperature.
